title: Shallow Retention Along the Inner Bend
narrative_elements: Curved bank slowdown; sediment layering; root-held moisture; reflective still water
moral_note: Stability arises through repeated small continuities rather than forceful motion
incoming_transition_annotation: Introduces localized slowing that becomes structural rather than incidental, preparing the emergence of sediment-held continuity.

title: Air Moving Through Reeds Near the Narrow Channel
narrative_elements: Narrow stone channel; reed flexing; intermittent wind; fragmented reflections
moral_note: Gentle movement preserves balance without requiring resistance
incoming_transition_annotation: Re-expands flow from retention state into directional movement, introducing wind and narrowing geometry as organizing forces.

title: Late Light Along the Sediment Shelf
narrative_elements: Lower sun angle; exposed sediment ridges; cooling shaded water; persistent underflow
moral_note: Perception deepens when observation remains steady through transition
incoming_transition_annotation: Moves focus from mechanical interaction (wind/reeds) to optical continuity, introducing light as a structuring medium.

title: Moss Holding Moisture Beneath Fallen Bark
narrative_elements: Bark cover; moss retention; shaded soil; slow decomposition integration
moral_note: Preservation often emerges through shelter rather than resistance
incoming_transition_annotation: Shifts perceptual emphasis from illuminated surface detail to shaded retention zones and peripheral moisture continuity.

title: Reflections Broken by Slow Surface Current
narrative_elements: Moving reflections; shallow stone interruptions; surface distortion; exposed roots
moral_note: Stability can exist within continual change when continuity is preserved
incoming_transition_annotation: Establishes parallel continuity between micro-retention systems and surface flow, reinforcing layered hydrological coherence.

title: Dimming Water Beneath the First Evening Coolness
narrative_elements: Fading light; cooling air; narrowing channel; reduced surface brightness
moral_note: Transition can occur through gradual reduction rather than decisive break
incoming_transition_annotation: Transitions from articulated surface perception to reduced-contrast continuity, initiating evening dimming phase without structural break.

title: Cooling Layer Above the Low Pool
narrative_elements: Low pool; cooling surface layer; stored stone warmth; darkened sediment shelf
moral_note: What remains steady can change register without losing direction
incoming_transition_annotation: Carries Anchor 54's evening reduction into a thermal register, preparing attention for cooling water, stored warmth, and low-pool continuity.

title: Pale Sky Held in the Narrow Run
narrative_elements: Narrow run; pale sky reflection; shallow edge stones; subdued surface ripples
moral_note: Even slight clarity has value when it remains faithful to what is present
incoming_transition_annotation: Moves from temperature-based perception into faint optical recurrence, linking the low pool to a narrow run where remaining sky becomes the next visible continuity.

title: Root Shadows Merging with the Bank
narrative_elements: Exposed roots; darkened bank soil; merged shadows; low current beside root structures
moral_note: The strongest forms of support need not announce themselves to remain essential
incoming_transition_annotation: Transfers focus from fading surface reflection to bank structure, preparing the root-shadow field of Anchor 57.

title: Dew Beginning on Low Grasses Beside the Creek
narrative_elements: Low grasses; early dew; damp soil boundary; creek sound nearby
moral_note: Small forms of return can renew a place without altering its quiet order
incoming_transition_annotation: Extends the bank's retained moisture into the surrounding low grasses, shifting from structural support to atmospheric condensation and edge continuity.

title: Small Sound Over Hidden Stone
narrative_elements: Submerged stone; low water sound; dark channel; repeated surface disturbance
moral_note: What cannot be fully seen may still be understood through attentive relation
incoming_transition_annotation: Draws the sequence from edge condensation back into audible flow, using submerged stone as the next marker of continuity.

title: Night Continuity Beneath the Still Canopy
narrative_elements: Still canopy; darkened channel; cooled banks; continuous low current
moral_note: Continuity does not require full visibility to remain whole
incoming_transition_annotation: Dissolves the localized sound of Anchor 59 into a broader nocturnal continuity, preparing Anchor 60's still canopy and sustained night flow.

title: Seepage Through the Gravel Margin
narrative_elements: Saturated bank gravel; lateral seepage; fine roots; gradual joining with the channel
moral_note: What sustains the whole may arrive quietly, through many small and careful passages
incoming_transition_annotation: Extends the nocturnal continuity of Anchor 60 into the bank itself, revealing quiet replenishment through soil and gravel rather than through the visible channel alone.

title: Leaf Drip Entering the Dark Surface
narrative_elements: Condensation on willow leaves; falling droplets; widening surface rings; steady subsurface current
moral_note: A balanced whole can receive what is offered without allowing any single addition to dominate it
incoming_transition_annotation: Carries the theme of quiet replenishment from hidden bank seepage to visible leaf drip, joining lateral and vertical returns of water within the same continuous system.

title: Waterline Along the Willow Root
narrative_elements: Exposed willow root; wet and dry bark boundary; fine sediment traces; slight current pulses
moral_note: Repeated contact can leave knowledge of change without damaging what bears the record
incoming_transition_annotation: Transforms the temporary surface rings of Anchor 62 into a persistent waterline, shifting attention from immediate contact to the physical record created by repeated contact.

title: Current Dividing Across the Submerged Gravel Bar
narrative_elements: Submerged gravel bar; divided current; interstitial flow; downstream rejoining
moral_note: Pressure is carried most safely when it is shared across many fitting paths
incoming_transition_annotation: Follows the recorded variations at the root back to their hydrological cause, moving from evidence at the bank to distributed flow across a submerged gravel structure.

title: Air Following the Channel Before Dawn
narrative_elements: Channel-guided cool air; shifting sedges; fern tips; elongated surface texture
moral_note: Clear direction can emerge from attentive relation to the conditions already present
incoming_transition_annotation: Carries the reunited water beyond the gravel bar and introduces a channel-guided movement of air, expanding continuity from hydrology into the surrounding atmosphere.

title: First Gray Across the Rejoined Current
narrative_elements: First pre-dawn reflection; rejoined current; recurring root and gravel forms; continued bank seepage
moral_note: A new interval begins most faithfully when it carries forward what quiet continuity has preserved
incoming_transition_annotation: Guides the sequence from pre-dawn atmospheric alignment into renewed visibility, bringing earlier motifs back into view while preserving their overnight continuity.

title: Sunlight Entering the Shallow Riffle
narrative_elements: Low-angle sunlight; shallow riffle; flat stones; alternating reflection and transparency
moral_note: Clear perception arises when movement and the forms guiding it are attended together
incoming_transition_annotation: Carries the renewed visibility of Anchor 66 into low morning sunlight, revealing a shallow riffle whose visible structure has persisted throughout the night.

title: Water Passing Beneath the Riffle Bed
theme: Reciprocity between visible and hidden flow
narrative_elements: Porous gravel; downward entry; interstitial passage; cool downstream upwelling
moral_note: Continuity is strengthened when what moves openly and what moves unseen remain in exchange
incoming_transition_annotation: Moves from the visible surface structure of the riffle into the hidden passage of water through its gravel bed, deepening the hydrological continuity beneath morning light.

title: Cool Seam Beneath the Alder Shade
narrative_elements: Gravel upwelling; alder shade; smooth surface seam; gradual current mixing
moral_note: Integrity allows distinct conditions to meet without requiring one to dominate the other
incoming_transition_annotation: Follows the hidden water of Anchor 68 into its downstream return, where a cool seam beneath alder shade reveals the gradual joining of distinct flow conditions.

title: Damselfly Resting Above the Current
narrative_elements: Folded transparent wings; bending sedge blade; reflected current; minute posture adjustments
moral_note: Presence can remain responsive without becoming forceful
incoming_transition_annotation: Carries the joined current beneath overhanging sedges and introduces a damselfly as a quiet living presence held within the creek's physical continuity.

title: Fine Roots Holding the Sedge Margin
narrative_elements: Fibrous sedge roots; saturated soil; capillary moisture; porous bank structure
moral_note: Lasting stability can arise from many small forms of support acting together
incoming_transition_annotation: Descends from the damselfly's sedge perch into the fibrous root network beneath it, shifting from visible responsiveness to distributed support within the bank.

title: Morning Widening Through the Creek Corridor
narrative_elements: Brightening canopy openings; recurring root and gravel forms; warmed surface; cool underflow
moral_note: A renewed interval remains whole by carrying forward the relations that made it possible
incoming_transition_annotation: Expands from the fine support system of Anchor 71 into a corridor-wide morning view, bringing recurring motifs together as parts of one continuing ecological relation.

title: Warmth Along the Exposed Stone Edge
theme: Uneven change held within one current
narrative_elements: Low morning sunlight; exposed flat stones; thin warmed surface water; cooler lower current
moral_note: Difference need not become division when exchange remains open
incoming_transition_annotation: Develops the increased visibility of Anchor 72 into a thermal relation, showing how sunlight produces local difference while continuous flow prevents separation.

title: Capillary Moisture Beneath the Moss Margin
narrative_elements: Shaded moss; fine soil pores; capillary rise; root and bark contact
moral_note: Sustaining movement can reach what direct flow does not
incoming_transition_annotation: Shifts from surface warming to capillary retention, following water from the visible channel into fine shaded spaces within the bank.

title: Light Passing Through the Alder Root Openings
narrative_elements: Submerged alder roots; open root arches; retained sediment; filtered morning light
moral_note: What endures can remain open to passage without surrendering its form
incoming_transition_annotation: Follows moisture through the bank into an alder root structure, revealing permeability as the condition that allows support and exchange to coexist.

title: Water Strider Crossing the Shaded Margin
narrative_elements: Water strider; surface-tension depressions; canopy reflection; slow marginal current
moral_note: A light presence can move through a shared field without taking more than it requires
incoming_transition_annotation: Moves from root-bound permeability to a water strider on the calm margin, extending the theme of passage into minimal living contact with the creek surface.

title: Cool Return at the Foot of the Gravel Shelf
theme: Hidden renewal within a warmed reach
narrative_elements: Hyporheic upwelling; gravel shelf; fine sand movement; gradual thermal mixing
moral_note: Renewal can strengthen the whole without demanding recognition of its source
incoming_transition_annotation: Uses the fading surface ripples of Anchor 76 to reveal a cool upwelling, redirecting attention from living contact to concealed hydrological renewal.

title: Midmorning Shade Returning Across the Channel
narrative_elements: Moving canopy shadow; heat retained in stone; cool underflow; recurring root and moss forms
moral_note: What returns is not repetition when every relation has continued to change
incoming_transition_annotation: Brings moving canopy shade across the warmed and replenished reach, gathering the sequence into a renewed balance without treating recurrence as reset.

title: Open Water Before the Crossing
narrative_elements: Open channel; irregular natural banks; approaching built geometry; uninterrupted sky above the current
moral_note: An existing presence remains whole even when another use of space begins to close around it
incoming_transition_annotation: Opens the burial sequence gradually, allowing built geometry to enter the creek corridor first at the margins while the water remains fully open to sky.

title: Banks Drawn In Around the Current
narrative_elements: Straightened margins; compacted ground; confined current; reduced lateral exchange
moral_note: Restriction begins at the edges long before it becomes complete
incoming_transition_annotation: Advances Stage 1 from approaching construction into physical confinement, emphasizing that burial begins through narrowing and edge control before overhead enclosure.

title: The First Roof Above the Creek
narrative_elements: Short overhead crossing; narrowed daylight; cooler enclosed air; reflected water sound
moral_note: What becomes less visible does not thereby become less present
incoming_transition_annotation: Introduces the decisive threshold of overhead construction while keeping the enclosure short, allowing the audience to experience burial first as the narrowing of sky.

title: Entering the Longer Covered Reach
narrative_elements: Culvert entrance; receding daylight; enclosed current; sustained downstream passage
moral_note: Continuity does not depend upon being continuously witnessed
incoming_transition_annotation: Converts the brief enclosure of Anchor 81 into the possibility of extended culverting, marking the point where crossing over the creek becomes building continuously above it.

title: Current Beneath the Built Surface
theme: Persistence beneath another use of place
narrative_elements: Buried channel; overhead load; lateral seepage; uninterrupted downstream current
moral_note: What is hidden from ordinary attention may remain essential to everything resting above it
incoming_transition_annotation: Deepens the enclosure into true built-overness, establishing the layered relation between the functioning surface above and the continuing watershed below.

title: Where the Creek Is No Longer Seen
narrative_elements: Continuous underground flow; uninterrupted surface above; absent visible banks; concealed downstream direction
moral_note: Absence from sight does not erase either existence or dependence
incoming_transition_annotation: Completes the first six-anchor burial sequence by moving from physical enclosure toward the beginning of cultural forgetting, preparing the next phase of decades-long buriedness.

title: Rain Reaching the Buried Channel
narrative_elements: Watershed rainfall; street drainage; groundwater contribution; rising underground current
moral_note: A living system may respond fully even when the response is hidden from ordinary view
incoming_transition_annotation: Begins the decades-long buried phase by showing that watershed events continue to register below the city even when the creek itself is absent from ordinary sight.

title: Seasonal Waterlines Beneath the Street
narrative_elements: Repeated high-water marks; seasonal discharge; drying wall surfaces; recurring sediment movement
moral_note: Time leaves knowledge in repeated contact even where no one is present to observe each event
incoming_transition_annotation: Moves from a single rainfall event into recurring seasonal cycles, establishing buriedness as a sustained condition measured through repeated hydraulic change.

title: Sediment Moving Through the Dark Reach
narrative_elements: Fine sand; gravel pockets; changing deposits; stronger-flow remobilization
moral_note: Continuity does not require materials to remain where they were
incoming_transition_annotation: Shifts from time recorded on enclosure walls to time recorded in the creek bed, emphasizing that sediment processes continue under burial.

title: Groundwater Entering at the Wall Seam
narrative_elements: Structural seam; groundwater seepage; mineral-darkened surface; quiet lateral inflow
moral_note: A relationship may persist through smaller openings even after its original form has been constrained
incoming_transition_annotation: Moves from sediment transport within the buried channel to groundwater exchange through structural seams, showing how an older bank relationship persists in altered form.

title: Ordinary Passage Above the Hidden Course
narrative_elements: Continuous built ground; repeated human passage; absent banks and waterline; active creek below
moral_note: What no longer interrupts attention can remain essential while gradually leaving ordinary awareness
incoming_transition_annotation: Moves from continuing subsurface exchange to the human condition above it, showing forgetting as a consequence of altered geography rather than conscious rejection.

title: The Grade Remaining Beneath Changed Surfaces
narrative_elements: Aging enclosure; repaired joints; changed surface uses; persistent downstream grade
moral_note: Continuity can outlast the forms built around it without remaining physically unchanged
incoming_transition_annotation: Extends buriedness across longer time by showing that infrastructure itself ages and changes while the creek's hydrological direction persists.

title: Water Sound Beneath the Drain Opening
narrative_elements: Drain opening; reflected water sound; rain entry; cool air rising from the buried channel
moral_note: Attention can recover a hidden relationship from small but truthful signs
incoming_transition_annotation: Begins the recognition phase through a small physical connection between surface and buried channel, allowing the creek to become perceptible without yet becoming visible.

title: The Low Line Across the Built Ground
narrative_elements: Subtle surface grade; repeated runoff path; drainage alignment; buried downstream direction
moral_note: What has been concealed can still shape the world around it
incoming_transition_annotation: Moves from immediate sensory recognition to spatial reasoning, allowing surface topography and drainage behavior to reveal the buried creek's continued direction.

title: Looking Into the Buried Reach
narrative_elements: Access opening; enclosed water surface; damp structural walls; visible downstream passage
moral_note: Seeing a condition clearly is not the same as repairing it, but clear witness can precede responsible change
incoming_transition_annotation: Carries indirect geographical recognition into direct observation of the buried channel through an access point, while maintaining the creek's underground condition.

title: Following the Buried Direction Beyond the Opening
narrative_elements: Access point; upstream inference; downstream alignment; repeated surface crossings
moral_note: Partial knowledge becomes useful when it is joined carefully rather than mistaken for the whole
incoming_transition_annotation: Expands recognition from one observed underground segment to the larger continuous buried course, reconnecting the visible glimpse with upstream and downstream watershed logic.

title: Ground Above Water
narrative_elements: Built surface; known buried alignment; unseen current; overlapping surface and creek geographies
moral_note: Accurate awareness can restore relationship before any physical restoration begins
incoming_transition_annotation: Shifts from reconstructing the buried alignment to the altered perception produced by knowing that the visible surface is only one layer of the site.

title: Measuring the Covered Reach
narrative_elements: Enclosure dimensions; structural edges; buried channel width; existing current beneath prospective opening
moral_note: Merciful change begins with understanding what is present before deciding what should be removed
incoming_transition_annotation: Carries recognition toward the first material possibility of daylighting, without beginning removal yet; the existing structure is newly perceived as alterable rather than permanent.

title: The First Section of Cover Removed
narrative_elements: Marked structural section; careful removal; exposed enclosure edge; uninterrupted current below
moral_note: Restoration can begin by removing what prevents an existing relationship from being perceived
incoming_transition_annotation: Moves from understanding the enclosure to the first physical act of daylighting, establishing removal of cover as the beginning of renewed access to an already-existing creek.

title: Daylight Reaching the Water
narrative_elements: Vertical opening; descending sunlight; illuminated wall surfaces; first direct light on moving water
moral_note: What becomes visible again carries the full history of the time when it could not be seen
incoming_transition_annotation: Carries the structural opening downward until daylight reaches the channel, marking the first direct reconnection between sky and buried water.

title: Air Entering the Opened Reach
narrative_elements: Open air circulation; changing humidity; exposed damp surfaces; moderated channel temperature
moral_note: Making room restores relationships that visibility alone cannot provide
incoming_transition_annotation: Expands the first return of light into renewed air exchange, showing daylighting as a physical environmental change rather than merely a visual one.

title: Space Returned Beside the Channel
narrative_elements: Widened opening; removed side constraint; exposed channel margin; developing bank slope
moral_note: Care can take physical form by allowing a living system enough space to maintain its relationships
incoming_transition_annotation: Moves from renewed atmospheric exchange to the physical widening required for banks and margins, shifting daylighting from exposure toward spatial restoration.

title: The First New Sediment Along the Open Bank
narrative_elements: Slower margin flow; fine sediment deposition; damp exposed soil; shifting gravel edge
moral_note: Renewal begins when contact becomes possible again
incoming_transition_annotation: Carries the widened opening into the first renewed bank-forming processes, showing water and sediment beginning to interact with a permeable margin.

title: The First Growth at the Reopened Margin
narrative_elements: Damp new sediment; first small plant growth; open air and light; continuing engineered remnants
moral_note: Mercy does not manufacture life; it creates conditions in which life can return by its own processes
incoming_transition_annotation: Extends renewed sediment and moisture into ecological possibility, carefully introducing biological return as gradual opportunity rather than immediate restoration.
